2021_171_m111720bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education meeting held November 17, 2020 by Zoom webinar, called to order by President Schmidt at 7:00 p.m. and adjourned at 8:45 p.m. with all seven members participating remotely from Troy, Michigan. The Board awarded two capital contracts — building signage to Johnson Sign Company for $92,000 inclusive of a 6% contingency, and school buses to Hoekstra Transportation for $1,687,276.00 — and adopted a resolution urging the Legislature to amend Senate Bill 1108 of 2020, which would restrict remote attendance by members of public bodies after December 31, 2020.
2021_171_m111720bdmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education, Board Meeting minutes, November 17, 2020, held remotely via Zoom Webinar with public notice posted for remote community participation. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.; adjournment at 8:45 p.m. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary (GH/jh).

**Attendance**
Present via Zoom videoconference in addition to Mr. Schmidt: Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson, all connecting from locations in Troy, Michigan. Also present: Superintendent Machesky; administrators Birmingham, Carrier, Griffor, DiPilato, Roncone, Haezebrouck, House, Pagel and West; two Student Board Reps; and approximately 48 additional members of the audience.

**Recognition — TSD Mission Moment**
The Michigan Council of Teachers of English (MCTE) Diversity, Inclusion, Justice, and Equity (DIJE) subcommittee awarded a DIJE professional development grant to Troy High School English teachers Jodie Duda, Erin Fischer-Ballew, Annie Gallagher, Christina Rick and Valerie Valentino. Their reading program includes "Black Appetite. White Food" by Jamila Lyiscott, "We Got This." by Cornelius Miner, "The Anti-Racist Teacher: Reading Instruction Workbook" by Lorena German, "Educating Activist Allies" by Katy Swalwell, and "Linguistic Justice" by April Baker-Bell.

**Public Communication**
Andrew Rodman, Troy resident and parent of two Martell Elementary School students, addressed the Board about moving elementary students back to remote learning and when they plan to return to in-seat instruction.

**Actions**

| No. | Item | Mover / Support | Vote |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20-084 | Consent agenda items A, B, C: minutes of the October 6, 2020 Workshop; minutes of the October 20, 2020 Board Meeting; Treasurer's Report - September 2020 | Hauff / Hammond | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 20-085 | Signage bid awarded to Johnson Sign Company, $92,000 (inclusive of 6% contingency), for refurbishment of the Athens High School messaging sign and new messaging signs at the Troy Preschool and Troy Learning Center; expenditure of the 2019 Capital Projects Fund and/or the Sinking Fund | Anne / Philippart | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 20-086 | School bus bid awarded to Hoekstra Transportation, $1,687,276.00, as an expenditure of the 2019 Capital Projects Fund | Philippart / Anne | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 20-087 | Reconfirmation of the District's COVID-19 Preparedness & Response Plan | Wilson / Philippart | Yes 6, No 1 (Hammond) |
| 20-088 | Resolution on Senate Bill 1108 / Open Meetings Act | Philippart / Hauff | Yes 7, No 0 |

**Discussion**
On the bus purchase, the Board discussed end of life cycle for buses and resale value, and grants for electric buses; Mr. West explained electric buses would be cost-prohibitive at this time. Dr. Machesky gave an extended learning plan update with PowerPoint slides on rising COVID case counts in Michigan and Oakland County, with additional updates from Ms. Birmingham, Mrs. Griffor and Mrs. DiPilato.

**Open Meetings Act resolution (20-088)**
Citing Governor Whitmer's framework and the Americans with Disabilities Act reasonable accommodation clause, the resolution urges the Legislature to amend Senate Bill 1108, Sec. 3a(b) so local public bodies set their own remote-participation policies, or at minimum to extend remote attendance for medical conditions and states of emergency or disaster in addition to military service, and directs the Board Secretary to transmit copies within five business days to Senator Mallory McMorrow, Representative Padma Kuppa, Oakland Schools Intermediate School District, and the Michigan Association of School Boards.

**Comments and reports**
Board comments from Hammond, Wilson, Philippart (TFEE raffle for $1,000 worth of gift cards, tickets $5 each), Gottlieb, Hauff and Anne. Student representatives Pranay Gupta (International Academy - East) and Nathania Nartey (Athens High School) reported; Sejal Patel (Troy High School) and Carleton Thomas (Troy College & Career High School) were not in attendance. Dr. Machesky congratulated Bemis Elementary School on a second National Blue Ribbon School recognition. Mr. Schmidt announced the next Board Workshop for December 1 at 6:00 p.m. via Zoom.
2021_171_m111720bdmtg.verbose:
Official minutes of a Board Meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, dated November 17, 2020, held remotely via Zoom Webinar. A public notice was posted to allow community members to participate remotely. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present via Zoom videoconference were Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson, all connecting remotely from locations in Troy, Michigan. Also present were Superintendent Machesky; administrators Birmingham, Carrier, Griffor, DiPilato, Roncone, Haezebrouck, House, Pagel and West; two Student Board Reps; and approximately 48 additional members of the audience. The minutes were submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the notation GH/jh.

RECOGNITION. The TSD Mission Moment honored the Michigan Council of Teachers of English (MCTE) Diversity, Inclusion, Justice & Equity (DIJE) Grant Award to Troy High School English teachers. The MCTE DIJE subcommittee awarded Jodie Duda, Erin Fischer-Ballew, Annie Gallagher, Christina Rick and Valerie Valentino of Troy High School a DIJE professional development grant. The grant's goal is to support Michigan English teachers across the state as they engage in professional development they design that privileges diversity, inclusion, justice, and equity work. The five teachers created a program of reading and learning supporting their commitment to "disrupting stock stories, stereotypes, and westernized narratives." Their selected texts are "Black Appetite. White Food: Issues of Race, Voice and Justice Within and Beyond the Classroom" by Jamila Lyiscott; "We Got This.: Equity, Access, and the Quest to Be Who Our Students Need Us to Be" by Cornelius Miner; "The Anti-Racist Teacher: Reading Instruction Workbook" by Lorena German; "Educating Activist Allies: Social Justice Pedagogy with the Suburban and Urban Elite" by Katy Swalwell; and "Linguistic Justice: Black Language, Literacy, Identity, and Pedagogy" by April Baker-Bell. Their intention is to use the concepts and practice from the readings to plan learning for students to build community and engage in rich activist lives.

ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS: None.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION. Andrew Rodman, Troy resident and parent of two students who attend Martell Elementary School, addressed the Board about the decision to move elementary students back to remote learning and when they plan to return to in-seat instruction.

GENERAL - CONSENT AGENDA (Resolution 20-084). It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Hammond that the Troy Board of Education approve items A, B and C on the consent agenda: minutes of the October 6, 2020 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the October 20, 2020 Board of Education Meeting; and the Treasurer's Report for September 2020. On roll call vote, Schmidt, Wilson, Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff and Philippart all voted Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

PERSONNEL and CURRICULUM sections contained no items.

BUSINESS - Building Signage (Resolution 20-085). It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Philippart that the bid for signage for the refurbishment of the school messaging sign at Athens High School and new messaging signs at the Troy Preschool and Troy Learning Center be awarded to Johnson Sign Company in the amount of $92,000 (inclusive of 6% contingency), and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2019 Capital Projects Fund and/or the Sinking Fund. On roll call vote, Wilson, Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Schmidt all voted Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

BUSINESS - Bus Purchase (Resolution 20-086). It was moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Anne that the bid for school buses be awarded to Hoekstra Transportation in the amount of $1,687,276.00 and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2019 Capital Projects Fund. There was discussion about the end of life cycle for buses and how much money the District could sell them for, and about looking into grants for electric buses; however, Mr. West explained that electric buses would be cost-prohibitive at this time. On roll call vote, Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt and Wilson all voted Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

Public Communication on non-agenda items: None.

OTHER - Extended Learning Plan. Dr. Machesky shared an update on the District's extended learning plan and provided PowerPoint slides showing the most recent numbers in COVID cases and how much they had been climbing in Michigan and in Oakland County. Ms. Birmingham, Mrs. Griffor and Mrs. DiPilato also shared updates from their respective areas, followed by further discussion among Board members.

Reconfirmation of COVID-19 Preparedness & Response Plan (Resolution 20-087). The minutes recite that Governor Whitmer's Executive Order 2020-142 provides a structure to support all schools in Michigan as they plan for a return of Pre-K through Post High School education in the fall, and that under this order Michigan school districts must adopt a COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Plan laying out how they will cope with the disease across the various phases of the Michigan Safe Start Plan. Each district must submit a reconfirmation plan to its Board of Education for approval on a monthly basis, and once approved must post its Preparedness Plan on the district website home page for public access. It was moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Dr. Philippart that the Troy Board of Education approve the District's Reconfirmation of the COVID-19 Preparedness & Response Plan. On roll call vote, Gottlieb Yes, Hammond No, Hauff Yes, Philippart Yes, Schmidt Yes, Wilson Yes, Anne Yes. Yes: 6, No: 1.

Open Meetings Act Resolution (Resolution 20-088). It was moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mr. Hauff. The whereas clauses state that Michigan Senate Bill 1108 of 2020 amended the State's Open Meetings Act to restrict the reasons a member of a public body may attend a public meeting remotely beginning January 1, 2021; that advancing technology enabled school districts across the State to meet remotely during the COVID-19 pandemic, develop and implement plans to educate students safely and effectively, and ensure safe and effective public participation; that the restrictions in Senate Bill 1108 allow remote attendance after December 31, 2021 only for absence due to military duty; that threats to public health and other disasters will not vanish on December 31, 2020, and that contagious diseases, flooding, tornadoes, acts of terrorism or other causes occurring after that date could make it unsafe or impossible for public bodies to meet in person or for some members to attend in person; that not allowing an immune-compromised member of a public body to participate remotely would be a clear violation of the Reasonable Accommodation clause of the Federal Americans with Disabilities Act; and that decisions about situations meriting remote attendance are best determined by the local body and the community it represents rather than the State Legislature. The resolved clauses urge the Legislature ideally to amend Senate Bill 1108, Sec. 3a(b) to include a provision requiring local public bodies to set their own policies regarding remote meeting participation based on the needs and priorities of their own local communities rather than dictating universal policy without regard to local control; urge the Legislature at a minimum to amend Sec. 3a(b) to extend indefinitely its provisions allowing remote attendance to accommodate absence due to a medical condition or a statewide or local state of emergency or state of disaster, in addition to military service, and to add accommodations for family emergencies and work obligations; and direct the Board Secretary to transmit copies of the resolution within five business days of adoption to Senator Mallory McMorrow, Representative Padma Kuppa, Oakland Schools Intermediate School District, and the Michigan Association of School Boards. On roll call vote, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson, Anne and Gottlieb all voted Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

BOARD COMMENTS. Mrs. Hammond spoke about events during the last Board meeting, said it was unfairly presented, and stated she will continue to advocate for what she believes in. Dr. Wilson thanked teachers and administrators for their hard work. Dr. Philippart announced that the TFEE is holding a pandemic-safe fundraiser offering a raffle for $1,000 worth of gift cards, with tickets available at $5 each. Mr. Gottlieb thanked TSD staff and fellow board members. Mr. Hauff thanked veterans for their sacrifice and service, thanked the Central Office staff and teachers, and said oneTROY is the greatest school district in Michigan. Mrs. Anne thanked everyone for their work during difficult times.

REPORTS FROM STUDENT REPRESENTATIVES. Pranay Gupta, student representative from International Academy - East, reported on students learning virtually at his school. Nathania Nartey, student representative from Athens High School, reported on happenings now that students are 100% virtual. Sejal Patel, student representative from Troy High School, and Carleton Thomas, student representative from Troy College & Career High School, were not in attendance.

Dr. Machesky thanked the Board for its continued efforts and support of the LIVE program, congratulated Bemis Elementary School on being recognized as a National Blue Ribbon School for the second time, and wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving. Mr. Schmidt wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving and announced the next Board Workshop for December 1 at 6:00 p.m. via Zoom.

ADJOURNMENT. The meeting was adjourned at 8:45 p.m.

2021_172_m121520bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education meeting held December 15, 2020 via Zoom webinar, called to order by President Schmidt at 7:00 p.m. and adjourned at 8:10 p.m. Actions included approval of a consent agenda carrying the October 2020 Treasurer's Report and Budget Adjustment #1, eight new hires, and the appointment of Cornelius Godfrey as Supervisor for Educational Equity, Inclusion & Community Relationships effective January 18, 2021. A motion by Mrs. Hammond to obtain a second opinion on the propriety of a closed session passed 4-3, and the Board did not go into closed session on attorney-client privilege.

**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education, Board Meeting minutes, December 15, 2020, held remotely via Zoom Webinar with public notice posted. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.; adjourned at 8:10 p.m. Submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary (GH/jh).

**Attendance**
In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present via Zoom videoconference were Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson, all connecting from locations in Troy, Michigan. Also present: Superintendent Machesky; administrators Carrier, Griffor, DiPilato, Cross, Haezebrouck, Conaton, Harris and West; two Student Board Reps; and approximately 12 additional members of the audience.

**Recognition — TSD Mission Moment**
Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction Christine DiPilato, Director of Teaching & Learning Natalie Haezebrouck, and Curriculum & Instruction Specialist for Social Studies Evan Rokicki introduced Zach MacIntosh, eighth grade teacher at Baker Middle School, named the 2020 Michigan History Teacher of the Year. The award is presented annually by the Gilder Lehrman Institute of American History. Official minutes of a Board Meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, dated December 15, 2020, held remotely via Zoom Webinar. A public notice was posted to allow community members to participate remotely. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present via Zoom videoconference were Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson, all connecting remotely from locations in Troy, Michigan. Also present were Superintendent Machesky; administrators Carrier, Griffor, DiPilato, Cross, Haezebrouck, Conaton, Harris and West; two Student Board Reps; and approximately 12 additional members of the audience. The minutes were submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the notation GH/jh.

RECOGNITION - TSD Mission Moment. Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction Christine DiPilato, Natalie Haezebrouck, Director of Teaching & Learning, and Evan Rokicki, Curriculum & Instruction Specialist for Social Studies, introduced Zach MacIntosh, eighth grade teacher at Baker Middle School, who was named the 2020 Michigan History Teacher of the Year. The award is presented annually by the Gilder Lehrman Institute of American History, described as the nation's leading organization dedicated to American history education; each year the institute selects one exceptional K-12 American history teacher from finalists in each state. In 2012 Zach received his bachelor's degree from Oakland University and began teaching history in the fall of 2012. In 2015 he received his Master's Degree from Saginaw Valley State University and followed up with an Education Specialist Degree in 2019 from Arkansas State University. His passion for history and technology have been combined in his classroom with an eye toward making history relevant to the younger generation, and he has built lasting relationships with students in the Troy School District around history as they critically analyze the American past. Zach was congratulated by all Board members and District administrators.

ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS: None.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION. Dr. Beth Feiten, Director of the School and Field Services Office (Student Teaching Office) of Oakland University, thanked the District administration, teachers and staff for their support and partnership during the pandemic.

GENERAL - CONSENT AGENDA (Resolution 20-089). It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Anne that the Troy Board of Education approve items A, B, C and D on the consent agenda: minutes of the November 10, 2020 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the October 17, 2020 Board of Education Meeting; the Treasurer's Report for October 2020; and Budget Adjustment #1. On roll call vote, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson, Anne and Gottlieb all voted Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

PERSONNEL - Elementary and Secondary (Resolution 20-090). It was moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Dr. Philippart that the Board of Education approve the personnel recommendations as stated, comprising New Hires Michelle Goleski, Katharine Sutherland, Corinn Puzzuoli, Rachel Williams, Raquel Cardenas, Kennedy Offman, Courtney Quade and Keegan Demar. On roll call vote, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson, Anne, Gottlieb and Hammond all voted Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

PERSONNEL - Administrative Appointment, Supervisor, Educational Equity, Inclusion & Community Relationships - C. Godfrey (Resolution 20-091). It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Philippart that the Board of Education approve Mr. Cornelius Godfrey, who will begin his duties as Supervisor for Educational Equity, Inclusion & Community Relationships on January 18, 2021. On roll call vote, Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson, Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond and Hauff all voted Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

CURRICULUM: None. BUSINESS: None. Public Communication on non-agenda items: None.

OTHER - Extended Learning Plan. Dr. Machesky had technical difficulty and was unable to share slides containing the most recent numbers in COVID cases in Michigan and in Oakland County, so he encouraged the community to visit the District's website to view updated information and current COVID data. He added that no changes were being recommended at that time for the Return to Learn Plan; however, the District would seek input from the parent community in early January about returning students to school and would also discuss plans at the January workshop. He recommended that the current plan be reconfirmed by the Board.

Reconfirmation of COVID-19 Preparedness & Response Plan (Resolution 20-092). The minutes recite that Governor Whitmer's Executive Order 2020-142 provides a structure to support all schools in Michigan as they plan for a return of Pre-K through Post High School education in the fall, and that under this order Michigan school districts must adopt a COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Plan laying out how they will cope with the disease across the various phases of the Michigan Safe Start Plan. Each district must submit a reconfirmation plan to its Board of Education for approval on a monthly basis, and once approved must post its Preparedness Plan on the district's website home page for public access. It was moved by Mr. Gottlieb and supported by Dr. Philippart that the Troy Board of Education approve the District's Reconfirmation of the COVID-19 Preparedness & Response Plan. On roll call vote, Schmidt Yes, Wilson Yes, Anne Yes, Gottlieb Yes, Hammond No, Hauff Yes, Philippart Yes. Yes: 6 (Schmidt, Wilson, Anne, Gottlieb, Hauff, Philippart), No: 1 (Hammond).

REPORTS FROM STUDENT REPRESENTATIVES TO THE BOARD. Nathania Nartey, Student Representative for Athens High School, shared an update on happenings in her school. Pranay Gupta, Student Representative for the International Academy-East, shared an update on what had been happening in his school. Sejal Patil, Student Representative for Troy High School, and Carlton Thomas, Student Representative for Troy College & Career High School, were not in attendance.

BOARD COMMENTS. Dr. Wilson thanked the administrators, teachers and the Baker team for the job they are doing and mentioned the learning opportunity MASB classes provide for Board members to engage with people across the state. Mr. Hauff shared a warm holiday message for administrators, teachers and students. Mr. Gottlieb wished everyone a Merry Christmas and Happy Hanukkah. Mrs. Anne thanked the schools, administrators, teachers and staff for their hard work and wished everyone happy holidays. Mrs. Hammond wished everyone happy holidays, talked about the CBA weekend at MASB, and mentioned solar energy other districts are using, suggesting the student representatives look into it further for debate and discussion at a future workshop. Dr. Philippart thanked the community for supporting the TFEE Raffle, sharing that they sold 1,000 tickets, which allows the foundation to fund grants for teachers, and thanked everyone for their work in trying circumstances. Dr. Machesky again welcomed Mr. Cornelius Godfrey to the District, thanked the unsung heroes who have helped support the District during the pandemic, and shared the passing of Pete Maurer, retired Baker Middle School teacher, extending condolences to Pete's family. Mr. Schmidt wished everyone happy holidays and shared his gratitude for everyone and for the students.

CLOSED SESSION - Attorney-Client Privilege (Resolution 20-093). It was moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Anne that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), the Troy Board of Education go into closed session to discuss an attorney-client privilege. Mr. Schmidt asked the Board if anyone had questions. Mrs. Hammond made a motion to get a second opinion on whether or not it was appropriate for the Board to go into closed session to discuss sale of property; Mr. Gottlieb supported the motion. On roll call vote, Anne Yes, Gottlieb Yes, Hammond Yes, Hauff Yes, Philippart No, Schmidt No, Wilson No. Yes: 4 (Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff), No: 3 (Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson). The motion passed 4-3 and the Board did not go into closed session to discuss an attorney-client privilege. Mr. Gottlieb recommended that administration find an attorney who has expertise in the area of the Open Meetings Act and closed session; administration will seek counsel regarding the issue and will hold a special meeting to discuss the issue at hand.

ADJOURNMENT. The meeting was adjourned at 8:10 p.m.
